raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Seasoning Blend
raw_recipe.description: DIY chicken seasoning? It’s easy! This go-to recipe blends herbs and spices you probably have on hand. It’s irresistible on poultry and much more.

video.description: The chicken seasoning in this video is a dry mix of herbs and spices that adds a unique zing to any poultry dish. It has just the right amount of heat and flavor to make your guests beg for more. Don't be scared by the long ingredient list!
video.name: Chicken Seasoning Blend Recipe

raw_recipe.name: Chicken Seasoning Blend

recipeInstructions.text: Mix salt, basil, rosemary, garlic powder, mustard powder, paprika, black pepper, thyme, celery seed, parsley, cumin, cayenne pepper, and chicken bouillon together in a small bowl until blended.
Use immediately or store in an airtight container for future use.

review.reviewBody: What a great combination of herbs and spices, all perfectly suited for one another! I haven't used this yet but if the aroma is any indication of how it's going to taste on the chicken breasts that are waiting for it we're in for a fine dinner! (I sheepishly confess that I wimped out on the cayenne pepper to be on the safe side and only used half the amount called for) Update: Used this on "Baked Lemon Chicken with Mushroom Sauce," which took this recipe from "blah" to sublime. I know I'm gonna love this stuff.

This was AMAZING! The blend of herbs and spices was Right On! I made 60 servings right off to bat and put the mix in an air tight container. I used this on 2 whole chickens and baked in the oven. I figured if some one did not like the taste then I was safe by just pulling off the skin. Everyone liked it. I can't wait to try it on skinless chicken breasts next.

Delicious without being overpowering; I placed six chicken breasts in a pyrex baking dish and drizzled them with olive oil. I put the seasoning blend into a shaker and sprinkled the breasts on both sides. Popped them into a 350 degree oven for about 45 minutes and they turned out juicy and very tasty. Great recipe!

other than the boullion granules, it is an excellent rub to use on chicken to have put on and sealed in a sealer bag for a few hours or overnight before smoking. To eat that evening. Not cured, but mmmm mmmmm tasty. thank you. like this rub. and adding the rosemary is a real bonus, goes well with pork loin also. minus the granules. the granules are good for the backing or frying. mmmmm chili? mmmm have to try that one. sounds good.
This spice rub has a lovely flavour, but even with 1/3 the salt is way too salty on baked chicken breast! Cut the salt to 1/4 tsp and it would be perfect!
AWESOME!! I had everything except the Celery Seed, but substituted Celery Salt and left out the Sea Salt.

Made exactly as is, but using the salt from a package for pretzels. (Not sure what's different about sea salt other than it's coarse.) It was very good, but not really what I expected. There's a lot of "Italian" type stuff in it, but the tiny bit of cumin and cayenne came through making a spicer vs herbier sort of flavor. But good. And of course, how can you really get any easier? I stored it away to keep for my don't-feel-like-it nights (which seem to be a lot anymore). I rubbed it on boneless chicken breasts -- first time pan fried them, and second time broiled them. The fried was definitely better, though I did go a little overboard with the stuff that first time.

This was excellent. I did not include salt or bullion granules as I am on a low sodium diet. The flavor was still rich with the cayenne adding just the right warmth. I used this as a dry rub on chicken breasts I pan fried in preparation for inclusion in a shepherds pie. I added about 1 1/2 tsp of blend to the pie gravy. Wonderful. Great way to spice up a gravy.

I had everything except the mustard powder… I am under the weather but felt a lot of flavor. I will use leftover spices on another occasion. I used chicken thighs and potatoes and put everything on the slow cooker. My son loved it. I have a sensitive stomach so I will use less next time.

Best chicken rub recipe for thighs in a cast iron skillet. Preheat your oven to 450 degees Fahrenheit with your cast skillet in the oven. Generously apply rub to your chicken thighs 4-6 small thighs on both sides, please adjust the salt in the rub to your liking, I prefer doubling recipe but only use 1 teaspoon of salt. When your oven is preheated, take out your cast Iron skillet and add 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter, 2 sprigs of fresh rosemary, when the butter is fully melted, put your chicken thighs in, skin down, and put back in the oven for 23 minutes, flip, and keep them for an additional 20 minutes. Viola!

I start this blend with 1/4 cup dried chicken bouillon powder( the kind with no MSG) , I follow the recipe exactly. I put the rosemary, thyme and celery seed in my mortar and grind with pestle until rosemary is broken up and celery seed are very aromatic. Then I put it all in a shaker bottle to use at will.
My family loves this on roasted vegetables, chicken, crostini, everything. Thank you for this great recipe.
with all the ingredients already on hand in my pantry, I was glad to try this recipe! Why buy another bottle of seasoning, when you can easily mix it yourself, in the quantity you need?
This is great!

Family approved. I halved the cayenne powder and skipped celery seeds because we don't like it. Everything else was used as is. I rubbed 8 chicken thighs and 4 drumsticks with olive oil and 2x the recipe and let it sit for 30 min before baking for 1 hr and finishing with the convection setting. Turned out perfect! Definitely a keeper.
Made exactly like the recipe. Love it!
Just added a little sage, otherwise perfect!
I was quick and easy to make! My husband had 3 pieces of chicken! I will be making it again in the future!
My husband said this was better than KFC!!
Measurements would be nice!?
EXCELLENT! A HUGE SUCCESS!
